analyst.summary: Bharti Airtel's FY26 results show real structural improvement -- net debt/EBITDA down to ~1.1x, capex intensity past its peak, FY26 operating FCF above Rs 41,500 crore, home broadband growing 31%+ YoY, and a 2.5-player market (Vi structurally propped up by government equity conversion, not competitively healthy) that keeps the industry aligned on tariff repair. But the 15.7% consolidated revenue headline is flattered by Indus Towers consolidation and Africa dollar-translation gains -- core India mobile revenue grew a more modest 7.7% YoY, ARPU rose only 4.9% YoY (lapping the last hike, not a new one), enterprise revenue was flat-to-down for the full year, and the next tariff hike (the market's central re-rating catalyst) has not yet been announced. At ~42-44x trailing earnings and ~10x book, the stock already prices in a lot of the good news building here. No balance-sheet or governance red flag, but full valuation and an unexecuted key catalyst argue for Hold, not for adding, and not for selling a fundamentally sound quality compounder into strength.
